subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: After fixing proposal-only Crestodian turns, should direct first installs from arbitrary npm, npm-pack, git, local path/archive, and marketplace sources require explicit acknowledgement while ClawHub, bundled, official-catalog, setup, repair, and update flows remain exempt?
rationale: The mandatory CLI contract and trusted-source exemptions define security and upgrade behavior; source correctness alone cannot establish the intended product boundary.

options.title: Approve narrowed gate
options.body: Keep the acknowledgement requirement for direct first arbitrary-source installs after repairing host rendering and proving the complete source matrix.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Do not merge the mandatory acknowledgement until a different provenance boundary or rollout strategy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Approve narrowed gate
recommendation.body: Keep the acknowledgement requirement for direct first arbitrary-source installs after repairing host rendering and proving the complete source matrix.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history makes Peter the strongest available owner of both the Crestodian approval lifecycle and central plugin-install behavior.
